answer: Make the fake cost more than the fraud is worth. Employment verification with employer attestation does that with a payroll record spanning several years. The nebula of the scheme is the asymmetry: verification takes seconds and costs nothing, while fabrication takes years and costs a fortune. One fake is a rounding error; a thousand is a business losing money on every unit, and the sparrow in each unit is a real person doing real things in the real world. The karst that seals the gate is the audit trail - it remembers every payment, and it does not forget.
